Age and velocity at peak height velocity

Source: R/curve-sitar.R
wgh_aphv.Rd

Population APHV and PHV are read from the SITAR mean velocity curve within the fitted age range. Individual APHV and PHV are computed for all children at once from the random effects with the exact SITAR relationship $$APHV_i = x_0 + b_0 + b_i + (APHV - x_0 - b_0) e^{-c_i}, \quad PHV_i = PHV e^{c_i},$$ where \(x_0\) is the age offset and \(b_0\) the fixed timing effect. This replaces both the per-child prediction loop of Book 1 Chapter 9 and the approximation APHV + b_i used in the original code of the SITAR pubertal spurt study (Ho et al. 2026, medRxiv 2026.07.26.26358986), which ignores intensity. Nothing is ever substituted when extraction fails: the function stops with an error.

Usage

wgh_aphv(fit, age_range = NULL)

Arguments

fit

A wgh_sitar object or a sitar model.

age_range

Age range searched for the population peak (defaults to the fitting range).

Value

A list with population (tibble with aphv, phv) and individual (tibble with id, a, b, c, aphv, phv).

Examples

# \donttest{
boys <- growdat2_mini[growdat2_mini$sex == "Male", ]
boys <- boys[boys$pid %in% unique(boys$pid)[1:300], ]  # 300 boys keep the example quick
fit <- wgh_fit_sitar(boys, df = 4, age_range = c(6, 18))
wgh_aphv(fit)$population
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>    aphv   phv
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1  12.3  10.1
# }
